subject.title: Feature request: MEMORY.md size warning/limit enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw add core Control UI save-time `MEMORY.md`/bootstrap-file budget enforcement and an archive workflow, or limit this issue to existing diagnostics plus the broader bounded-memory design?
rationale: Current main already warns and diagnoses truncation, but the remaining request changes workspace-file editing UX and memory lifecycle rather than repairing one established code path.

options.title: Define a narrow core UX contract
options.body: Add a Control UI budget display and explicit save-time warning/blocking for bootstrap files, while leaving auto-archive to a separate memory design.

options.title: Fold into bounded memory work
options.body: Track hard limits and archive behavior in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42877 and use this issue only for the Control UI diagnostics slice if maintainers want it separate.

options.title: Limit to diagnostics
options.body: Treat current prompt, doctor, and `/context` visibility as sufficient unless a maintainer sponsors UI save enforcement.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core UX contract
recommendation.body: Add a Control UI budget display and explicit save-time warning/blocking for bootstrap files, while leaving auto-archive to a separate memory design.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the central bootstrap truncation warning/reporting surface and are the strongest history-backed owner for deciding how far the core UX should extend.
